name: create_figure
description:
Create an empty figure and return its figure_id. Start here.

Use rows/cols for a grid of panels; address a panel with `panel=N` in later calls.

name: describe_figure
description:
List open figures, or describe one: its artists and what each panel currently shows
(axis limits, labels, legend entries). Cheaper than render_figure and returns no image.

figure_id.description: Figure to describe; omit to list all open figures.

name: close_figure
description: Close a figure and free its data. Datasets are kept.

name: create_dataset
description:
Create (or replace) a named table of equal-length numeric columns.

Expressions are evaluated safely (no attribute access, no builtins) with numpy
functions such as sin, exp, sqrt, linspace, arange, noise(n, scale, seed); see
glplot://guide for the full list. Use this instead of typing out data points.

Example: create_dataset("run", {"t": "linspace(0, 10, 500)", "v": "sin(t)*exp(-t/5)"}).

columns.description: Ordered map of column name -> list of numbers OR an expression string over earlier columns, e.g. {'t': 'linspace(0, 10, 500)', 'y': 'sin(t)*exp(-t/5)'}. Column names must be identifiers.

base.description: Start from this dataset's columns; new columns may use them.

name: load_dataset
description:
Load a CSV/TSV/TXT, NPY/NPZ, JSON or image file as a dataset.

The first row is used as column names when it is a header. Text columns become categories
(labels kept; see select_rows and analyze_dataset 'aggregate') and ISO date columns become
days since 1970-01-01. A 2-D .npy becomes one column per array column. Returns the
columns with min/max/mean/std and the first rows.

path.description: File inside the server's allowed directory (relative or absolute).

name.description: Name to give it; default: file name.

name: describe_dataset
description: Show a dataset's columns, per-column statistics and first rows, or list all datasets.

name.description: Dataset to describe; omit to list all datasets.

name: analyze_dataset
description:
Analyse a dataset numerically and keep the result so it can be plotted. Operations: describe (report); fit (column); smooth (column); rolling (column); derivative (column); integrate (column); fft (table); peaks (table); filter (column); detrend (column); normalize (column); resample (table); histogram (table); correlate (report); aggregate (table); autocorrelation (table).

A 'column' result is added to the dataset (e.g. v_fit), a 'table' result becomes a new dataset (e.g. run_fft), a 'report' only returns numbers. The reply includes a plot_hint with the add_plot call that draws it. fit supports linear, polynomial, gaussian, lorentzian, exp_decay, power_law, sigmoid, multipeak and custom expressions, and reports parameters with standard errors and R^2. Options per operation: get_guide('mcp-analysis').

Examples: analyze_dataset("run", "fit", x="t", y="v", options={"model": "exp_decay"}); analyze_dataset("signal", "fft", x="t", y="v"); analyze_dataset("run", "smooth", y="v", options={"window": 31}).

operation.description: One of: describe, fit, smooth, rolling, derivative, integrate, fft, peaks, filter, detrend, normalize, resample, histogram, correlate, aggregate, autocorrelation. get_guide('mcp-analysis') lists each one's options.

y.description: Column to analyse. Default: the only column that is not x.

x.description: x column (the abscissa). Default: the row index, i.e. unit spacing. Required by correlate.

options.description: Operation-specific options, e.g. {'model': 'exp_decay'} for fit, {'method': 'savgol', 'window': 31} for smooth, {'cutoff': 5} for filter. Unknown names are refused with the valid ones listed.

output.description: Name for the column (same-length results) or the new dataset (tables) to create. Default: <y>_<suffix> or <dataset>_<operation>.

name: select_rows

where.description: Keep rows where this expression over the columns is true, e.g. 'temp > 10' or '(temp > 10) & (year == 2021)' (use & | ~ with parentheses, not and/or/not).

equals.description: Keep rows whose column equals a value or any of a list: {'city': 'Lima'} or {'city': ['Lima', 'Oslo']} for a text (category) column, {'year': 2021} for a numeric one.

sort_by.description: Column to sort the kept rows by (NaN last).

every.description: Keep every n-th of the remaining rows.

limit.description: Keep only the first n rows (after sorting).

output.description: Name of the new dataset. Default: <dataset>_rows.

name: delete_dataset
description: Delete a dataset. Figures already drawn from it keep their picture.

name: add_plot
description:
Draw data as a line, scatter, bar, histogram, box, pie, ... and return an artist_id.

Each kind needs different series; the per-kind table is in glplot://guide. Options a
kind does not use are ignored and listed in the reply. Returns the artist_id used by
remove_artist.

Examples: add_plot("fig1", "scatter", x=[1, 2, 3], y=[2, 4, 9], color="red");
add_plot("fig1", "line", dataset="run", x="t", y="v", label="run");
add_plot("fig1", "hist", dataset="run", y="v", bins=30).

kind.description: One of: line, scatter, step, stem, bar, barh, area, errorbar, hist, box, violin, pie, hist2d, hexbin. See the table in glplot://guide.

dataset.description: Dataset that column-name arguments refer to.

x.description: A column name (requires `dataset`) or a short list of numbers; null in a list is a gap. Prefer column names for anything over ~100 values.

y.description: A column name (requires `dataset`) or a short list of numbers; null in a list is a gap. Prefer column names for anything over ~100 values.

z.description: Third coordinate. Required on a 3-D figure (line/scatter only).

error.description: +/- size for errorbar (per point or a single number) and bar.

columns.description: box/violin: dataset columns, one box per column.

color.description: Colour name ('red'), hex ('#1f77b4') or 'tab:blue'. Default: next in cycle.

color_by.description: scatter: values mapped through `cmap` to colour each point.

size_by.description: scatter: values mapped to marker size.

cmap.description: Colormap for color_by / hist2d / hexbin, e.g. 'viridis'.

size.description: Marker size in px (line markers, scatter).

tick_labels.description: bar/barh: category names under the bars; pie: slice names.

panel.description: Panel number in a multi-panel figure, 1-based, row-major. Leave at 1 for a single-panel figure.

hatch.description: bar/barh/area/hist fill pattern: '/', 'x', '+', '.', 'o', '//' (a backslash pattern works too).

axis.description: 'left' (default) or 'right': draw against a second y axis on the right (line, scatter, step, bar, area, errorbar). Label it with set_axes(y2label=..., y2lim=...).

reveal.description: Show only the first fraction (0-1) of the points: a curve drawing itself in. Bind it to time in animate. line/scatter/step/bar/area/errorbar.

trail.description: Show only the last N of the revealed points: a moving tail.

head.description: Put a dot on the last shown point (line/scatter/step): the 'head'.

name: add_function
description:
Plot y = expression(x) over [x_min, x_max] in one call, without making a dataset.

The quickest way to draw a formula or to overlay several (call it once per curve).

Example: add_function("fig1", "sin(a*x)/x", x_min=-10, x_max=10, parameters={"a": 2}).

expression.description: y as a function of x, e.g. 'sin(a*x)/x'. Parameters go in `parameters`.

x_min.description: Left end of the x range.

x_max.description: Right end of the x range (> x_min).

parameters.description: Named constants usable in the expression, e.g. {'a': 2}.

label.description: Legend text. Default: the expression itself.

color.description: Colour name ('red'), hex ('#1f77b4') or 'tab:blue'. Default: next in cycle.

panel.description: Panel number in a multi-panel figure, 1-based, row-major. Leave at 1 for a single-panel figure.

name: add_field
description:
Draw a 2-D scalar field z(x, y) as an image, contours, or a 3-D surface.

Give exactly one source: `expression`, `matrix` or `file`.

kind.description: One of: image, contour, contourf, pcolormesh, surface, wireframe (surface/wireframe need a 3-D figure).

expression.description: z in terms of x and y, e.g. 'sin(x)*cos(y)'.

matrix.description: Small inline grid, rows of numbers (row 0 = lowest y).

file.description: A 2-D .npy file or an image file in the allowed directory.

resolution.description: Cells per side for `expression` (default 200; 80 for surfaces).

vmin.description: Value mapped to the low end of the colormap.

vmax.description: Value mapped to the high end of the colormap.

panel.description: Panel number in a multi-panel figure, 1-based, row-major. Leave at 1 for a single-panel figure.

name: list_recipes
description:
List the ready-made recipes: what each draws, the columns (slots) it reads, its look.

A recipe is a plot kind *and* the look it was designed in (palette, colormap, page,
3-D camera), so it is the quickest route to a figure that already looks good.

category.description: Only this category: Lines, Scatter, Density, Bars, Fields or 3D.

name: add_recipe
description:
Draw a ready-made recipe (plot kind + look) from a dataset, or from its sample data.

Axis names come from the column names, the page and colours from the look. Returns an
artist_id (for remove_artist) and the columns it used. A 3-D recipe needs a figure
created with projection='3d'. Add titles, limits and a legend with set_axes afterwards.

dataset.description: Dataset to draw from (create_dataset / load_dataset). Omit with sample=true.

columns.description: Slot -> column overrides, e.g. {'y': 'signal', 'c': 'age'}. Columns are guessed from their names; use '(index)' for the row number and null to empty a slot. Only what you want to change.

sample.description: Use the recipe's own example table instead of a dataset (it is added as a dataset).

look.description: 'recipe' (its own page and palette, default), 'keep' (the figure's current look) or a style key such as 'journal' or 'dark'.

label.description: Legend text for this series. Omit and it stays out of the legend.

panel.description: Panel number in a multi-panel figure, 1-based, row-major. Leave at 1 for a single-panel figure.

name: add_annotation
description: Add a text note, a horizontal reference line (at y) or a vertical one (at x). 2-D only.

color.description: Colour name ('red'), hex ('#1f77b4') or 'tab:blue'. Default: next in cycle.

panel.description: Panel number in a multi-panel figure, 1-based, row-major. Leave at 1 for a single-panel figure.

name: remove_artist
description: Remove what one add_* call drew (or everything). Use after render_figure shows a mistake.

artist_id.description: Artist to remove, e.g. 'a2'. Omit to remove everything.

name: set_axes
description:
Set title, axis labels, limits, scales, grid, legend and (3-D) camera on one panel.

Pass only what you want to change. Always label axes with units.

Example: set_axes("fig1", title="Decay", xlabel="t (s)", ylabel="signal (V)", yscale="log",
legend=True).

panel.description: Panel number in a multi-panel figure, 1-based, row-major. Leave at 1 for a single-panel figure.

legend.description: True to show a legend of labelled series.

equal_aspect.description: Same units per pixel on x and y.

hide_axes.description: True to hide the axes (images, pies).

y2label.description: Label of the right-hand y axis (after add_plot(axis='right')).

y2lim.description: [low, high] of the right-hand y axis.

y2scale.description: Scale of the right-hand y axis: 'linear', 'log'...

name: set_style
description: Apply a style preset (background, palette, line width, grid) to the whole figure.

name: render_figure
description:
Render the figure and return it as an image plus a text summary of each panel's axes.

Look at the image and the summary (axis limits, labels, legend) before telling the
user it is done; fix problems with set_axes / remove_artist / add_*.

The reply also reviews the figure and lists `issues` it can prove (missing axis labels or
title, an empty panel, overlapping tick labels, points a log axis cannot draw, data cut off
by the limits...), each with a severity and the call that fixes it. An empty list means
nothing was found.

params.description: Control values to render at, e.g. {'amp': 2, 'mode': 'cos'} (see add_control). The figure itself keeps its own values.

name: save_figure
description: Save the figure to a file. Refuses to overwrite unless overwrite=true.

path.description: Output file in the allowed directory; format from extension (.png .svg .pdf .jpg).

params.description: Control values to render at, e.g. {'amp': 2, 'mode': 'cos'} (see add_control). The figure itself keeps its own values.

name: update_artist

changes.description: Arguments of the call that drew it, with their new values: {'color': 'tab:red', 'linewidth': 3}. null puts one back to its default; 'parameters.a' reaches inside an object argument; {} redraws from the data.

name: add_control
description:
Define a slider, toggle, choice or button: a named value the figure can depend on.

A control does nothing until a property follows it: bind_property(figure, 'a1',
'linewidth', 'width'). Then set_control moves it and the figure is redrawn, render_figure
(params={...}) tries values without keeping them, animate can sweep it, and
export_script(kind='interactive') writes the real widgets as Python.

Example: add_control("fig1", "amp", min=0, max=5, value=1).

name.description: Identifier used in expressions (e.g. 'amp'). Not t, s, time, x, y.

kind.description: 'slider' (needs min and max), 'toggle' (true/false -> 1/0), 'choice' (needs options; its value in expressions is the option's index) or 'button' (sets other controls, or resets them all).

options.description: choice: two or more option names.

sets.description: button: {control: value} pairs it applies; omit to reset all.

name: set_control
description: Move a control (the figure is redrawn at the new value) or press a button.

value.description: New value (slider number, toggle true/false, choice option name). Omit for a button.

name: bind_property
description:
Make one property follow an expression of the figure's controls (and of time).

Bindings apply on every redraw and in `animate`. Names in the expression are control
names; inside animate also t (0..1), time (s), frame, s (stage progress) and variables.

Examples: bind_property("fig1", "a1", "parameters.amp", "amp");
bind_property("fig1", "axes", "title", {"format": "amp = {amp:.1f}"}).

target.description: What to drive: an artist id ('a1'); 'axes' or 'axes:2' (panel title, xlabel, xlim, ylim, zlim, elev, azim, legend...); or 'data:<dataset>' (then `property` is a column recomputed from the others).

property.description: The argument to drive: 'color', 'linewidth', 'alpha', 'size', 'reveal', 'trail', 'parameters.a' (a function's parameter), 'x_max', 'azim'...

value.description: A number, an expression of controls and time ('1 + 2*amp', 'sin(2*pi*t)'), a list of those ('xlim': ['0', '10*t']), {'colormap': 'viridis'|[colours], 'at': expr}, {'choose': [...], 'index': expr} or {'format': 'phase {time:.1f} s'}. null removes the binding.

name: animate
description:
Animate the figure: properties follow time, in stages, and save a GIF/MP4/WebM/PNGs.

You cannot watch an animation, so the reply is a contact sheet (frames side by side) plus
measured facts: variable ranges per stage and `issues` (nothing moves, the axes rescale,
the loop does not close, an abrupt jump). Build the figure first, pin the axes
(set_axes xlim/ylim), then say what varies: variables (+ stages) and bindings.
Preview with output omitted, fix, then write the file. Read get_guide('mcp-animation').

Example, a wave that travels, grows, then squeezes:
animate("fig1", output="wave.gif", fps=25, variables={"phase": "2*pi*t", "amp": 1, "k": 2},
stages=[{"name": "travel", "duration": 2}, {"name": "grow", "duration": 2,
"animate": {"amp": [1, 3]}}, {"name": "squeeze", "duration": 2, "animate": {"k": [2, 5]}}],
bindings=[{"target": "a1", "property": "parameters.phase", "value": "phase"},
{"target": "a1", "property": "parameters.amp", "value": "amp"},
{"target": "a1", "property": "parameters.k", "value": "k"}]).
3-D orbit: bindings=[{"target": "axes", "property": "azim", "value": "30 + 360*t"}].

output.description: File to write in the allowed directory: .gif, .apng, .mp4 or .webm (those two need ffmpeg), or 'frames/f_%04d.png' for numbered images. Omit to only preview: a contact sheet of frames is always returned.

loop.description: True for a seamless loop: t runs 0..1 excluding the end, so the last frame leads into the first. Use whole periods (2*pi*t).

stages.description: Consecutive stages, each {'name', 'duration' (s) or 'frames', 'ease', 'animate': {...}}. `animate` moves variables: {'amp': [1, 3]} (from, to), {'amp': 3} (to, from wherever it is), {'amp': {'from': 1, 'to': 3, 'ease': 'in_out'}} or {'k': '2 + 3*s'} (expression of s, 0..1 across the stage). A stage starts where the last ended and ends exactly on its target; afterwards the value holds. Easings: linear, in, out, in_out, smooth, smoother, sine.

variables.description: Named values: a NUMBER is a parameter (its starting value; stages may move it), an expression STRING is derived each frame from t, time, s, stage and the parameters: {'amp': 1, 'phase': '2*pi*t', 'w': '2*pi*f'}.

bindings.description: What the variables drive, [{'target', 'property', 'value'}] -- the same as bind_property (added to the figure's own bindings). value is an expression of the variables: {'target': 'a1', 'property': 'parameters.phase', 'value': 'phase'}; {'target': 'axes', 'property': 'azim', 'value': '30+360*t'}.

hold_start.description: Seconds to hold the first frame.

hold_end.description: Seconds to hold the last frame.

sheet_frames.description: Frames in the contact sheet returned.

frame.description: Render only this frame, full size (nothing is written).

repeat.description: GIF/APNG: extra plays after the first (0=forever).

name: simulate
description:
Integrate ordinary differential equations into a dataset (t, each state, derived).

For dynamics that are not a formula of t: a pendulum, predator-prey, Lorenz, an orbit, a
driven oscillator. Plot the result, and animate it with add_plot(reveal=..., head=true)
bound to time. Equations use the same safe expression language as everywhere.

Example: simulate("lorenz", {"x": "s*(y-x)", "y": "x*(r-z)-y", "z": "x*y-b*z"},
{"x": 1, "y": 1, "z": 1}, t_end=40, parameters={"s": 10, "r": 28, "b": 2.667}).

name.description: Name of the dataset to create.

equations.description: Each state's derivative as an expression of the states, t and the parameters: {'theta': 'omega', 'omega': '-g/L*sin(theta) - c*omega'}.

derived.description: Extra columns computed from the solution, e.g. {'energy': '0.5*omega**2 + g/L*(1-cos(theta))'}.

name: export_script
description:
Return the Python script that rebuilds this figure, to give the user to keep and edit.

Generated from the calls that built the figure; datasets are rebuilt from how they were
made (expressions -> numpy, simulate -> solve_ivp). The script is returned as text in the
reply (nothing is written to disk). Run it with python; it needs only glplot.

kind.description: 'figure' (the figure as it is now, saved to PNG), 'interactive' (controls become real sliders/toggles/menus/buttons that redraw it) or 'animation' (the last animate call as a FuncAnimation saved to GIF).

name: get_guide
description:
Read GLPlot's documentation: a guide topic as Markdown, or the list of topics.

Topics starting `mcp-` explain these tools; the others cover the Python API (plot types,
axes and styling, 3-D, animation, controls, performance, differences from matplotlib,
troubleshooting). Read the relevant one before writing a script or choosing a plot kind.

topic.description: Topic id, e.g. 'quickstart', 'three-d', 'animation', 'mcp-plot-kinds'. Omit to list every topic.

name: search_api
description:
Find GLPlot Python functions by name or by what they do (about 250 functions).

Returns each match's call shape and one-line summary. Follow up with get_api_doc for the
full docstring. Useful before writing a script, or to answer "can GLPlot do X?".

query.description: What you want to do or a name: 'heatmap', 'second y axis', 'error bars', 'save gif'. Empty lists every category.

category.description: Only this category id (figure, plot2d, fields, plot3d, axes, annotate, color, controls, output, signal, perf, interaction, compat).

name: get_api_doc
description:
The exact signature and full docstring of one GLPlot function (read from the code).

An unknown name returns near-miss suggestions.

name: get_example
description:
A complete runnable Python script using GLPlot, or the list of examples.

Every example ends in plt.savefig, so it runs with no display. Use one as the starting
point for a script rather than writing it from memory.

name.description: Example id, e.g. 'line_plot', 'surface_3d'. Omit to list them.

name: server_info
description: Versions, what this server may do (file roots, limits), and what is open now.
